subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI cross-channel observe/mirror mode, and should the first supported shape be read-only and visibility-scoped rather than interactive bidirectional mirroring?
rationale: The request crosses channel/session privacy boundaries and may add public CLI or config surface, so automation cannot safely choose the security policy or product shape.

options.title: Read-only scoped observe mode
options.body: Add an explicit opt-in observer that displays only sessions the operator is authorized to see, with clear agent, identity, channel, and session scope.

options.title: Interactive bidirectional mirror
options.body: Allow TUI to both observe and send across mirrored channels, accepting a larger delivery, message-loss, and privacy-policy surface before implementation.

options.title: Keep logs as workaround
options.body: Do not add core observer/mirror mode now and leave `openclaw logs --follow` plus explicit session selection as the supported monitoring path.

recommendation.title: Read-only scoped observe mode
recommendation.body: Add an explicit opt-in observer that displays only sessions the operator is authorized to see, with clear agent, identity, channel, and session scope.

likelyOwner.reason: They landed the isolation behavior that created the current product tradeoff and have recent TUI session lifecycle ownership signals.
